title: Cost Model API SLOs and Error Budget Policy
author: Sean Gallagher
body:
h1. Overview
The Cost Model API (service: *cost-model-service*) provides deterministic cost estimates and explainable cost attribution breakdowns for Redwood Console and Optimize.

This page defines:
* Production SLIs/SLOs (availability and latency)
* Error budget policy and release guardrails
* Alert thresholds and paging policy based on dependency criticality

The Cost Model API is *not* the source of truth for billing/invoicing (see PRD). SLOs are tuned to minimize impact to:
* *Console* cost breakdown pages (interactive, user-facing)
* *Optimize* scenario sweeps (batch/offline, recommendation quality)

h2. Service scope
h3. In-scope endpoints (prod)
* *Estimate*: POST /cost-model/estimate (and versioned variants)
* *Explain / attribution*: POST /cost-model/explain
* Health: GET /healthz, GET /readyz (for orchestration; not counted in SLOs)

h3. In-scope environments
* Production (Hosted, Dedicated, and Private control planes where operated by Redwood)
* SLO compliance is tracked per region and aggregated globally.

h3. Out of scope
* Staging/dev
* Client-side latency (SDK/network) and downstream Console page rendering
* Telemetry freshness SLOs (tracked separately by Telemetry Platform)

h2. Users and dependency criticality
h3. Criticality tiers
|| Consumer || Usage pattern || User impact if degraded || Required behavior ||
| Console (cost breakdown UI) | Interactive; frequent reads on page load and drill-down | Medium-to-high (page shows partial data; support volume increases) | Must have safe fallback (cached breakdown or “estimated unavailable” state) | 
| Optimize (what-if sweeps) | Batch jobs; scenario sweeps; can retry/backoff | Medium (recommendations delayed; should not produce misleading results) | Must gate on confidence and retry; never block core product traffic | 
| Internal tooling | Ad-hoc | Low | Best-effort | 

h3. Dependency notes
* Console can tolerate short outages if cached responses exist (recommended TTL 5–15 min; see integration how-to). However, repeated timeouts can degrade the page and drive support escalations.
* Optimize must treat low-confidence or assumption-heavy results as non-actionable and avoid emitting definitive savings claims.

h2. SLIs (what we measure)
All SLIs are measured at the Cost Model API ingress (gateway or service mesh) in *prod*.

h3. Availability SLI
*SLI definition:* proportion of valid API requests served successfully.

* Good events: HTTP 2xx.
* Bad events: HTTP 5xx, gateway 504/524, and explicit internal timeout responses.
* Excluded from SLI (do not count as good or bad):
  * HTTP 4xx due to client input validation (400, 422)
  * HTTP 401/403 (authn/authz)
  * HTTP 404 (route not found)
  * HTTP 429 (rate limit) — tracked separately as a capacity signal; not used to “hide” outages

Notes:
* We track excluded classes separately; a spike in 4xx is an integration quality issue and can still alert (see Alerting).
* Version negotiation failures ("unsupported_version") are counted as 4xx and excluded from availability but should page the owning team if persistent.

h3. Latency SLIs
*SLI definition:* request duration from first byte received to last byte sent by cost-model-service.

We report p50/p95/p99. SLOs are set on p95 and p99.

Latency is tracked by endpoint family:
* *Estimate latency* (POST /estimate)
* *Explain latency* (POST /explain)

Requests with extremely large payloads (above documented limits) are rejected by validation and excluded from latency SLOs.

h2. SLOs (targets)
All SLOs are defined over a rolling *28-day window*.

h3. Availability SLO
|| SLO || Target || Window || Notes ||
| Cost Model API availability | *99.90%* | 28 days | Aggregated across all in-service regions; also monitored per region for localized failures | 

Interpretation:
* 99.90% allows ~43.2 minutes of error budget per 30 days (approx). We use a 28-day window for burn calculations.

h3. Latency SLOs
We set separate latency SLOs to reflect different compute paths.

|| Endpoint || p95 target || p99 target || Window ||
| /estimate | *150 ms* | *350 ms* | 28 days |
| /explain | *250 ms* | *600 ms* | 28 days |

Notes and rationale:
* /explain may resolve additional metadata (model catalog, quant profile details) and returns richer payloads for Console tooltips.
* If /explain is frequently called in bulk (anti-pattern), owners must implement batching/caching or move workloads to /estimate.

h3. SLO exclusions and segmentation
We also segment SLO compliance by:
* Region
* Deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Global SLO is the release gate; regional SLOs are used for incident detection and routing.

h2. Error budget policy
h3. Ownership
* Primary SLO owner: *Eng SRE* (Neha Kapoor, Sean Gallagher)
* Service owner: *Eng Platform / Control Plane* (Priya Natarajan, Ethan Park)

h3. Error budget burn response
If error budget burn exceeds thresholds, the following rules apply:

1) *Fast burn (paging)*
* Trigger: Availability burn rate >= 14x over 1 hour (see alerting)
* Action: Incident declared; mitigate (rollback, disable feature flags, reduce load, fail open to cached values in clients).

2) *Sustained burn (freeze consideration)*
* Trigger: Availability burn rate >= 2x over 6 hours OR latency burn rate >= 2x over 6 hours
* Action: Service owner and SRE decide whether to pause non-critical deploys to cost-model-service and dependent callers (Console/Optimize) until burn stabilizes.

3) *Budget exhausted*
* Trigger: Remaining availability error budget < 10% in current window
* Action: Freeze “non-essential” changes to cost-model-service (new features, refactors) and prioritize reliability work. Exceptions require approval from Neha Kapoor (SRE) and Priya Natarajan (Platform owner).

h3. Release guardrails
* Any change affecting calculation paths, downstream dependencies, or request validation must ship behind a feature flag with canary.
* Canary must include:
  * Latency regression check (p95 and p99)
  * Error rate check (5xx + timeouts)
  * Mismatch detector (estimated vs metered attribution drift) where applicable
* Rollout should be staged by tenant/tier when feasible.

h2. Alerting and paging
We use multi-window, multi-burn alerts (Google SRE pattern) and separate page vs ticket thresholds.

h3. Availability alerts
*Page (P1) – fast burn*
* Condition: burn rate >= 14x over 1h AND >= 14x over 5m
* Expected impact: Console degradation, Optimize retries/backlog, elevated support contacts
* On-call: Eng SRE (primary), Eng Platform (secondary)

*Page (P2) – sustained burn*
* Condition: burn rate >= 6x over 6h AND >= 6x over 30m

*Ticket (P3) – slow burn*
* Condition: burn rate >= 1x over 3d

h3. Latency alerts
Latency alerts are per endpoint family.

*Page (P2) – p99 latency regression impacting Console*
* /estimate p99 > 600 ms for 15m OR /explain p99 > 1000 ms for 15m
* Additionally requires request volume above baseline minimum (avoid paging on low-traffic noise)

*Ticket (P3) – sustained p95 creep*
* /estimate p95 > 200 ms for 6h OR /explain p95 > 350 ms for 6h

h3. Integration-quality alerts (non-SLO but actionable)
* High validation failures: 4xx (400/422) > 2% for 30m (ticket to owning client team: Console or Optimize)
* Unsupported version errors: “unsupported_version” > 0.5% for 30m (ticket to Platform + client owner)
* Rate limiting: 429 > 1% for 15m (investigate capacity, client retry storm, or missing caching)

h3. Dashboard links (Grafana)
Dashboards are managed in observability-pack; canonical panels:
* cost-model-service Overview (availability, latency, saturation)
* Endpoint breakdown (/estimate vs /explain)
* Regional heatmap
* Dependency correlation: Console error rates vs SCM latency
* Mismatch detector: estimated vs metered attribution drift

(See: confluence://eng-sre/dashboards/cost-model-service)

h2. Incident response notes
h3. Common failure modes and mitigations
* Downstream dependency slowdown (model catalog / telemetry lookups)
  * Mitigate: enable internal caching, degrade to “assumption mode” with explicit confidence impact, increase timeouts carefully
* Thundering herd from Console after deploy
  * Mitigate: enforce client caching, add request coalescing, raise circuit-breakers at gateway
* Validation rejects missing fields (e.g., region)
  * Mitigate: hotfix to accept safe defaults only if it does not break determinism guarantees; otherwise update clients
* Version negotiation mismatch
  * Mitigate: server-side fallback to supported version where allowed by conventions; coordinate with client release

h3. Client fallback expectations
* Console must:
  * Use cached response when available
  * Render an explicit “Cost breakdown temporarily unavailable” state (not $0)
  * Avoid repeated synchronous retries on page load
* Optimize must:
  * Retry with exponential backoff
  * Avoid publishing recommendations when SCM confidence is low or assumptions are too coarse

h2. Capacity and scaling signals (operational)
We track, but do not SLO-gate on:
* CPU/memory saturation of cost-model-service
* Internal cache hit ratio (request memoization / shared cache)
* Queueing/admission control metrics
* Per-tenant spikes (with cardinality controls)

If 429s occur, treat as a capacity/abuse signal and investigate whether clients are missing caching or sending excessive scenario sweeps.

h2. Change log
* 2025-03-06: Updated latency SLOs to separate /estimate and /explain; clarified 429 exclusion policy; added integration-quality alerts.
* 2025-02-18: Initial publication of availability and baseline latency targets; adopted burn-rate alerting pattern.
